newsitem.title: USA: Shuffle Master rejects merge talks.
newsitem.headline: Shuffle Master rejects merge talks.

text.p: Shuffle Master Inc., which provides gambling products for the casino industry, said Monday it rebuffed an unsolicited approach from Anchor Gaming on a possible merger, and expected Anchor to challenge one of its patents.
The Minneapolis-based company said Stanley Fulton, Chairman and CEO of Anchor Gaming, had approached Shuffle Master about a business combination. Shuffle Master said it would not pursue such talks.
Shuffle Master said it believed Anchor Gaming would file a suit charging that Shuffle Master's "Let It Ride" game infringes on patents held by Anchor.
Shuffle Master Chairman John Breeding, said if a lawsuit were filed, it would be "a blatant attempt" to pressure his company into an agreement with Anchor.
He said that if a suit were filed Shuffle Master would seek damages and try to invalidate Anchor's patents by asking the U.S. Patent and Trademark Office to reexamine Anchor's patents.
The news sent Shuffle Master's stock up 50 cents to $12.25 in early afternon trading on the Nasdaq, while the stock of Anchor Gaming fell $1.875 to $51.50.
